provenance.author: block writer B7 (Claude Opus 5.5, model-written)
notes: Short future: the four irregulars are productive in 1sg, 2sg and 1pl (af i/ei di/awn ni; gwnaf i/gwnei di/gwnawn ni; caf i/cei di/cawn ni; dof i/doi di/down ni), with wna i ddim and the yes-answers Af / Gwnaf. Regular -af (cymeraf i, gwelaf i, gwasgaf i) appears only in Rhita's boasts, glossed '= bydda i'n …', receptive. No 3sg short future is used: third persons keep bydd (Bydd Pero'n dod; Fydd e ddim yn marw), which Pensum A a7 contrasts.
Written affirmatives keep -f (gwnaf i, af i, as in the plan); the negative follows the plan's spoken wna i ddim. Pensa accept both gwnaf/gwna and wna/wnaf. See review question on s_wna1.

Promotions at 37: mor … â used productively (mor wyn â'r eira, mor fach â llygoden, mor fawr â thŷ, mor uchel â tharanau, mor fach ag wy); the other conditional persons used (baset ti, basech chi, basen ni, basen nhw).
Dafi's one deliberate error (Gwnaf i mwg) contrasts with the SM after the short future and is corrected in the next line by Mali (Gwnaf i fwg).
No open-slot words: neb (Pennod 26) and llawer (Pennod 32) are already introduced by parallel writers' open slots and are recycled here.

Continuity choices: the summit party is Arthur, Cai, Mali, Dafi and Pero; Myrddin climbs part-way, refuses to use magic ('Chi sy'n mynd i'r copa, dim fi') and arrives only after the cairn is built. The shepherd's rope comes from Pennod 36's hut. Cai wears Modlen's wool beard (34) and Rhita blows it away. Mali recovers the lock of Cynyr's beard (33). The giant is not killed: he falls on the summit, sleeps, and is buried asleep under a cairn (sets up the sleeping-king image of 40).
Cai's victory boast (s_boast) and his promise to tell the story in the Caerllion tavern, against Mali's 'Y stori go iawn', set up Pennod 38.
Known checker behaviour: phrase lexemes (ar fy mhen fy hun, gyda'n gilydd) may be reported against their component words; prose was not distorted to avoid it.

review_questions.question: [?] Short future register: written gwnaf i / af i in affirmatives but spoken wna i ddim in negatives (as the plan lists). Better to write wnaf i ddim throughout, or gwna i / a i throughout?
[?] 'a doi di gyda ni, Mali' — is doi di natural southern, or would learners hear do i / doi di as dei di?
[?] 'Cei di aros yn y sach' / 'cei di frathu'r cawr' for 'you may …' (permission): natural?
[?] 'Ei di'n gyntaf' (you'll go first): natural, or prefer 'Cei di fynd yn gyntaf'?
[?] ffêr gender (plan: f.) and 'ei ffêr e' with no mutation.
[?] 'gwnaf i ddweud y stori' as a simple future of dweud: natural, or prefer 'bydda i'n dweud'?
[?] 'Baset ti'n ymladd ar dy ben dy hun, tasai dewrder gyda ti!' — tasai with a noun subject and gyda-possession: natural?
[?] 'mor fawr â chychod' (as big as boats, plural cychod): natural?

primary_new_grammar.label: Short-form future of mynd, gwneud, cael, dod: af i / ei di / awn ni; gwnaf i / gwnei di / gwnawn ni; caf i / cei di / cawn ni; dof i / doi di / down ni; wna i ddim; Wnei di …? — Gwnaf; SM after the short future (Gwnaf i fwg). Regular -af (cymeraf i, gwelaf i) and 3sg receptive.

cover.alt: The giant Rhita Gawr looms out of thick mist on the summit of Yr Wyddfa, his cloak of beards blowing, while Arthur, Cai and Mali, roped together, climb the last rocks below with old Pero.
cover.art_brief: The summit of Yr Wyddfa in thick grey mist (Eryri palette: mist greys, wet slate, a cold pale light). Looming out of the mist above, huge and only half visible, Rhita Gawr (match char-rhita.png: giant three times a man's height, bald dome, bushy black eyebrows, big red nose, his own long dark-brown beard, rough fawn tunic with rope belt, big brown boots) with his long cloak of stitched beard-tufts in red, gold, slate-blue, brown and grey (no faces) stirring in the wind; vain smirk. Below him on a steep rocky path along a cliff edge: Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with cowlick, freckles, moss-green tunic, plain blue cloak, no crown) in front, Cai (15, red-blond, rust-red tunic, sword and round shield) and Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, satchel and a cloth sack on her back) behind, all three tied together by one long brown rope; old Pero (shaggy black-and-white hound, grey muzzle) labouring up beside Arthur; a tiny red head with cream horns (Dafi) peeping from the sack. Far below, on a rock at the edge of the mist, the small figure of Myrddin (tall black brimmed hat) sits watching. Absolutely no text.

segments.text: Bore oer oedd hi yn Eryri: roedd y storm eira wedi mynd, ond roedd niwl llwyd, trwm ar yr Wyddfa, a doedd neb yn gallu gweld y copa.
Gadawodd Arthur, Cai, Mali a Myrddin fwthyn y bugail yn gynnar.
Roedd Pero'n cerdded yn araf wrth draed Arthur, ac roedd Dafi'n cysgu yn sach Mali, gyda'r bara.
Roedd rhaff hir, gryf gyda Mali hefyd: rhaff y bugail.

inference_aids.label: rhaff
inference_aids.art_brief: A long coil of rough brown shepherd's rope, knotted at one end. Ink line and watercolour, transparent background, no text.

segments.text: "Af i'n gyntaf," meddai Cai.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Fi yw'r marchog, a fi yw'r cryfaf."

segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "Dw i ddim yn gweld dim byd yn y niwl."

segments.text: "Af i gyda Cai, a doi di gyda ni, Mali, gyda'r rhaff."

Ond eisteddodd Myrddin ar graig wrth y llwybr, ac roedd ei het ddu'n wlyb yn y niwl.
"Af i ddim i'r copa," meddai e.
segments.speaker: char-myrddin

segments.text: "Dw i'n hen, ac mae'r llwybr yn serth. Bydda i'n aros yma, wrth y graig."
"Ond dewin dych chi!" meddai Cai.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Basech chi'n gallu taflu'r cawr i'r môr gyda hud!"
"Gallwn i," meddai Myrddin. "Ond wna i ddim."
segments.speaker: char-myrddin

segments.text: "Heddiw, does dim hud. Chi sy'n mynd i'r copa, dim fi."
Edrychodd e ar Arthur dros ei sbectol, ac roedd e'n gwenu. "Wyt ti'n cofio'r gwyddau?"
"Ydw," meddai Arthur. "Dylai brenin arwain fel gŵydd."
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Gwnaf i rywbeth defnyddiol, felly," meddai Mali, a chododd hi'r rhaff ar ei chefn.
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: Yn sydyn, daeth pen bach coch o'r sach, gyda bara ar ei drwyn.
"A fi?" meddai Dafi. "Beth wna i?"
segments.speaker: char-dafi

segments.text: "Cei di aros yn y sach, Dafi," meddai Mali.
segments.speaker: char-mali

inference_aids.gloss: caf i · cei di · cawn ni

segments.text: "Wna i ddim aros yn y sach!" meddai Dafi. "Mae'r bara wedi mynd!"
segments.speaker: char-dafi

segments.text: Dringodd y tri'n araf drwy'r niwl.
Doedd neb ar y llwybr, dim ond y tri ffrind a Pero.
Roedd y llethr yn serth, ac roedd creigiau gwlyb a cherrig rhydd ar y llwybr.
Weithiau roedd Cai'n cwympo ar ei drwyn, a weithiau roedd Pero'n eistedd i lawr ac yn edrych ar Arthur gyda llygaid trist.
Ar ochr y llwybr roedd clogwyn uchel, ac roedd niwl gwyn yn y cwm dan y clogwyn.

segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Dw i ddim yn edrych i lawr," meddai Mali.
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "Ti sy'n edrych i lawr, Cai, ac rwyt ti mor wyn â'r eira."

segments.text: "A Pero?" meddai Mali.

segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: Ar ôl awr hir, clywon nhw sŵn o'r copa: llais mawr, dwfn, fel taran.

"Pwy yw'r cawr mwyaf yn y byd? Fi!"
segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: "Pwy yw'r cawr cryfaf yn y byd? Fi!"
"Pwy sy â'r clogyn gorau yn y byd? Fi, fi, fi!"

"Mae e'n canu amdano fe!" meddai Cai yn dawel.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Mae e'n falch iawn," meddai Mali. "Mae e mor falch â brenin."
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "Awn ni i fyny'n dawel," meddai Arthur.
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Paid â thisian nawr, Dafi."
Ar y copa, roedd llai o niwl.
A dyna fe, ar garreg fawr: Rhita Gawr.
Roedd e'n anferth: roedd ei draed e mor fawr â chychod, ac roedd ei ben e yn y cymylau.
Roedd e'n gwisgo clogyn hir o farfau: barfau coch, barfau du, barfau llwyd a barfau aur.
Roedd e'n edrych ar ei glogyn ac yn gwenu fel plentyn gyda phastai.
"Mae e'n anferth!" meddai Cai yn dawel.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Mae e'n fwy na'r neuadd yng Nghaerllion!"

inference_aids.alt: Rhita Gawr sits on a boulder on the misty summit of Yr Wyddfa admiring his long cloak sewn from many coloured beards, while Arthur, Cai and Mali, roped together, peer at him from behind a rock with old Pero; a little red dragon looks out of Mali's sack.
inference_aids.art_brief: The summit of Yr Wyddfa in thinning mist (Eryri palette: mist greys, wet slate, a little pale sky). Rhita Gawr (match char-rhita.png: giant three times a man's height, bald dome, bushy black eyebrows, big red nose, his own long dark-brown beard, rough fawn tunic with rope belt, big brown boots) sits on a great boulder, holding up a corner of his long cloak made of rows of stitched beard-tufts (red, gold, slate-blue, brown, grey, no faces) and admiring it vainly. In the foreground behind a wet grey rock: Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with cowlick, moss-green tunic, plain blue cloak, no crown), Cai (15, red-blond, rust-red tunic, sword and round shield) and Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, satchel) tied together by one brown rope; old Pero (black-and-white shaggy hound, grey muzzle) crouching; Dafi (cup-sized red dragon, cream horns, yellow eyes) peeping out of a cloth sack on Mali's back. segments.text: "Dyma farf brenin Iwerddon," meddai'r cawr.
segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: "A dyma farf brenin Llydaw. Mae llawer o farfau ar fy nghlogyn i. A dyma farf newydd: barf Cynyr, arglwydd Cwm Helyg! Barf hir, barf aur, barf dda!"
"Barf Dad!" meddai Mali yn dawel, ac roedd dagrau yn ei llygaid hi.
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: Yn sydyn, cododd y cawr ei drwyn mawr coch ac arogli'r gwynt.
"Dw i'n arogli dynion bach!" meddai e. "Dewch yma, ddynion bach!"
segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: Daeth Arthur o'r graig yn araf.
Roedd ei galon e'n curo, ond roedd ei lais e'n dawel.
"Arthur dw i," meddai e. "Fi yw'r brenin newydd."
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: Rhuodd Rhita Gawr, a chwympodd cerrig bach i lawr y llethr.
"Ti? Y brenin newydd? Rwyt ti mor fach â llygoden!"
segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: "Wel, frenin bach: cymeraf i dy farf di!
Gwelaf i hi ar fy nghlogyn i yfory!"
Plygodd e i lawr, ac edrychodd e ar wyneb Arthur am amser hir gyda'i lygaid bach.
"… Ond does dim barf gyda ti!"
Yna daeth Cai o'r graig hefyd, ac roedd barf wlân fawr ar ei wyneb e: barf ffug Modlen.
"Fi yw'r brenin!" meddai Cai yn uchel. "Dyma fy marf i!"
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: Edrychodd y cawr ar y farf wlân, ac yna ar wyneb coch Cai.
"Barf wlân? Barf ffug!" meddai Rhita. "Basai dafad yn gwybod hynny!"
segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: Rhuodd e eto, a hedfanodd y farf wlân i'r niwl.
"Fy marf i!" meddai Cai.
segments.speaker: char-cai

sections.title: Wna i ddim ymladd ar fy mhen fy hun

segments.text: Safodd Rhita Gawr ar ei draed, ac roedd ei ben e uwchben y niwl.
"Brwydr, felly!" meddai e.
segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: "Ti a fi, frenin bach, ar dy ben dy hun!"
"Baset ti'n ymladd ar dy ben dy hun, tasai dewrder gyda ti!"
"Wna i ddim ymladd ar fy mhen fy hun," meddai Arthur.
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Dyn ni'n ffrindiau, ac awn ni i'r frwydr gyda'n gilydd."
"Gyda'n gilydd?" Rhuodd y cawr eto.
segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: "Llygoden, merch fach, hen gi a marchog heb farf!"
"Rwyt ti'n fwy na fi," meddai Arthur.
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Ond gyda'n gilydd, dyn ni'n fwy na ti."
Cododd Rhita garreg mor fawr â thŷ, a thaflodd e'r garreg.
Hedfanodd y garreg dros eu pennau nhw, i'r niwl, ac i lawr y clogwyn.
"Mae e'n taflu cerrig!" meddai Cai.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Gwasgaf i chi fel wyau!" rhuodd y cawr.
segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: Rhedodd y plant yn ôl at y graig, a chuddion nhw yno gyda Pero.
Doedd dim angen y rhaff ar y tri nawr, a chododd Mali hi ar ei chefn eto.
"Gwnaf i ymladd!" meddai Cai, ac roedd ei gleddyf e yn ei law.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Af i at ei draed e, a gwnaf i dorri ei esgidiau e!"
"Aros, Cai," meddai Arthur. "Mae cynllun gyda fi."
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Dafi, wnei di fwg i fi? Mwg mawr, du?"
"Gwnaf i mwg mawr iawn!" meddai Dafi.
segments.speaker: char-dafi

segments.text: "Gwnaf i fwg, Dafi," meddai Mali. "Fwg!"
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "Gwnaf i fwg mawr iawn," meddai Dafi, ac roedd e'n hapus.
segments.speaker: char-dafi

segments.text: "Mali, ei di at y clogwyn gyda'r rhaff?"
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Af," meddai Mali.
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "Os bydd e'n cerdded at y clogwyn, gwnaf i ei faglu e."

segments.text: "O! O! Fy ffêr i!"
segments.speaker: char-rhita

inference_aids.alt: In the smoky mist on the summit the giant topples backwards: Dafi's black smoke round his eyes, Pero biting his ankle, his other boot caught on Mali's rope stretched between two rocks, and Cai and Arthur pushing at his side with their shoulders.
inference_aids.art_brief: Comic action on the misty summit of Yr Wyddfa (mist greys, wet slate). Rhita Gawr (match char-rhita.png; beard cloak of coloured beard-tufts, no faces) toppling over backwards, arms flailing, eyes screwed shut in a cloud of thick black smoke from tiny Dafi (cup-sized red dragon, cream horns) who hovers by his nose mid-sneeze; old Pero (shaggy black-and-white hound) hanging on to the giant's bare ankle above his big brown boot; the giant's other boot snagged on a brown rope tied between two rocks, Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress) crouching by one rock holding the rope taut; Cai (15, red-blond, rust-red tunic) and Arthur (12, cowlick, moss-green tunic, blue cloak) shoving at his side with their shoulders. inference_aids.alt: Late afternoon on the summit: everyone piles stones on the sleeping giant to make a cairn; Cai carries a big stone, Arthur and Mali smaller ones, Dafi a pebble the size of an egg, Pero curled asleep on the growing heap, and Myrddin coming up the path below with the last golden light.
inference_aids.art_brief: The summit of Yr Wyddfa late in the day, the mist lifting into gold and grey light (Eryri palette). A long low cairn of grey stones covers the sleeping giant; only the tip of his big red nose and one big brown boot still show. Cai (15, red-blond, rust-red tunic) heaves a large stone, grinning; Arthur (12, cowlick, moss-green tunic, blue cloak) and Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress) carry smaller stones; Mali has a folded bundle of the beard cloak at her feet. Dafi (cup-sized red dragon, cream horns) flies with a pebble no bigger than an egg towards the giant's nose. Old Pero (shaggy black-and-white hound) is curled asleep on top of the cairn. segments.text: Pan oedd yr haul yn mynd i lawr, roedd y garnedd yn barod: carnedd anferth, ar ben yr Wyddfa.

"Buddugoliaeth!" meddai Cai, ac roedd e'n dawnsio ar y cerrig.

segments.text: "Brwydr fawr, a buddugoliaeth fawr! Bydd y beirdd yn canu am y frwydr hon am flynyddoedd!"

segments.text: Penliniodd Arthur wrth y garnedd, a rhoddodd e ei law ar y cerrig oer.

segments.text: "Ond gwnaf i addo: bydd dy enw di ar y mynydd."

segments.text: Gwenodd Myrddin, ond doedd e ddim yn dweud dim byd.

Yn bell yn y de, dan y cymylau, roedd Cwm Helyg.
"Pryd awn ni yn ôl i Gaerllion?" meddai Cai. "Dw i eisiau bwyd."

segments.text: "Yfory," meddai Arthur. "Awn ni yn ôl yfory, gyda'n gilydd."

grammar.nodyn_en: Short future of four common verbs: af i (I'll go), gwnaf i (I'll do/make), caf i (I'll get; also 'may'), dof i (I'll come), with ei/gwnei/cei/doi di and awn/gwnawn/cawn/down ni. It means the same as bydda i'n … . What follows softens: Gwnaf i fwg. Negative: Wna i ddim. Speech often drops the -f: gwna i, a i.
